name: Amazon RDS
oneLiner: You rent the instance by the second plus storage and backups, whether it serves a query or sits idle.
trap: Multi-AZ replication traffic itself is free, but your app crossing an AZ to reach the DB is not. Multi-AZ still doubles instance and storage cost and doubles write I/O.

name: Amazon Aurora
oneLiner: Instance-hours plus storage, and on Aurora Standard every storage I/O is its own line on the bill.
trap: Aurora Standard bills read/write I/O per million; I/O-Optimized deletes that meter but raises instance and storage rates. Cross-AZ replication is free, Global Database replication is not.

name: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2
oneLiner: Capacity billed by the ACU-second instead of the instance-hour.
trap: ACUs bill every second at your minimum even while idle, unless min capacity is 0 and auto-pause kicks in. Storage, I/O and transfer bill exactly as provisioned Aurora; only compute changes.

name: Amazon DynamoDB
oneLiner: The clearest case where your capacity mode decides which meter you are billed on at all.
trap: Provisioned RCU/WCU bill per hour whether you read a byte or not, so that is Time. On-demand RRU/WRU bill per request, so that is Calls. Same queries, different meter.

name: Amazon ElastiCache
oneLiner: Node-hours if you size the cluster yourself, or per-request ECPUs if you let it go serverless.
trap: On node clusters, app-to-cache traffic across an AZ is billed at EC2 rates. Serverless swaps node-hours for GB-hours plus per-request ECPUs, so the Calls meter only exists in that mode.

name: Amazon MemoryDB
oneLiner: Node-hours like any cache, plus a charge on every GB you write. Reads cost nothing extra.
trap: The data-written charge blindsides write-heavy workloads: it is per GB written, not per request, and reads are free. Only cross-region Multi-Region replication triggers data transfer.

name: Amazon Redshift
oneLiner: Node-hours plus managed storage, and Spectrum queries into S3 bill on their own by bytes scanned.
trap: Spectrum bills per byte scanned with a 10 MB minimum per query, and Concurrency Scaling bills per second past the free credits. Both are bundled into RPUs on Serverless.

name: Amazon Redshift Serverless
oneLiner: RPU-hours ticking per second while queries run, with a 60-second floor on every one of them.
trap: That 60-second minimum charge makes a stream of tiny queries cost far more than their runtime. Spectrum and Concurrency Scaling are included, so no separate per-query meter exists.

name: Amazon DocumentDB
oneLiner: Aurora's billing model in a MongoDB shape: instance-hours, storage, and I/O billed per million.
trap: I/O per million is the line people leave out when sizing. Cross-AZ replication for multi-AZ clusters is free, and elastic clusters bill vCPU-minutes instead of instance-hours.

name: Amazon Neptune
oneLiner: Instance-hours or NCU-hours, storage, and I/O per million unless you switch to I/O-Optimized.
trap: Neptune Standard bills I/O per million; I/O-Optimized zeroes that meter in exchange for higher instance and storage rates, and you can only switch between them once per 30 days.

name: Amazon Timestream
oneLiner: Two products now: LiveAnalytics is shut to new customers, so InfluxDB is the one you can actually start.
trap: LiveAnalytics closed to new customers on 2025-06-20. Its query meter is TCU-hours for newer accounts and bytes scanned for older ones; writes bill per KB ingested.

name: Amazon Keyspaces
oneLiner: Cassandra on DynamoDB-shaped billing: RRU/WRU when on-demand, hourly RCU/WCU when provisioned.
trap: Consistency level moves the bill: a LOCAL_ONE read costs half an RRU versus LOCAL_QUORUM. TTL deletes bill per KB per row, and multi-Region writes bill WRUs in every Region.

name: Amazon RDS Proxy
oneLiner: Priced off the size of the database it fronts, not off your traffic. No per-request charge at all.
trap: You pay per vCPU-hour of the underlying DB, or per ACU-hour for Aurora Serverless, even at zero connections. Read-only and read-write proxy endpoints add PrivateLink charges on top.
